name: Ragnheiður Oluwakemi-Tsiranov
role: hyperlane migrant; climate refugee from drowned coastal settlement, currently in transit
location: Grand Crossing Gate, temporary migrant processing zone, third holding section, near North Ave and Damen
description:
Ragnheiður is tall and angular, with pale skin that has burned and recovered enough times to have a permanent rosy-raw quality at her cheekbones and nose. Her hair is a natural deep auburn, grown out in a manner suggesting she has not had access to a proper cutting implement in months, pulled back in a knot held by what appears to be a sharpened stylus. Her eyes are grey-green and extremely direct — she has the look of someone who stopped performing social softness some time ago because it cost too much energy. She carries everything she owns in a single large waterproof pack with a broken clasp, fixed shut with cable ties. On her left wrist is a tattoo of a coastline — the actual coastline of the settlement she grew up in, measured and mapped by her own hand before the water took it — and she will show it to anyone who asks, with the precision of a cartographer or a mourner.

She is not the kind of refugee who presents with visible despair, which sometimes means aid workers overlook her in favor of more legible suffering. What she has instead is a particular flat-affect efficiency: she needs a specific set of things, she is working to acquire them through the specific channels available to her, and she would prefer not to waste either her time or anyone else's on anything peripheral to that. She was a coastal agricultural cooperative manager before her settlement was inundated — a competent, practical person with professional expertise that is almost entirely inapplicable to an urban megacity. She is learning this in real time and finds it enraging.

core_fears: losing the twelve people she has become responsible for to the processing system's inefficiencies
arriving somewhere permanent and discovering she cannot build anything there — that the loss has made her unable to start again
core_desires: work she is actually competent at — she wants to be useful again in the specific way she was useful before
coping_mechanisms: pragmatic task focus — converts grief into logistics
the notebook of complaints, which is also secretly a journal she would not describe as such
blind_spots: her flat affect reads as coldness or hostility to people who don't know her, and she does not compensate for this because she finds the work of managing others' perceptions of her exhausting and somewhat contemptible
has not yet fully grieved and will not function entirely correctly until she does
psychology.secret: She delayed the final evacuation of her settlement by eighteen hours arguing with a cooperative board member about asset documentation protocols. She believes those eighteen hours cost one person their life — an elderly man who was evacuated late and died of exposure during the transit. She does not know for certain that earlier evacuation would have saved him. She is not certain it would have. She thinks about it every day.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and direct. Cooperative management terminology. Becomes very formal when angry, which is counterintuitively more frightening than shouting.
speech_patterns.cadence: Even, controlled, with clipped endings. Does not trail off.
verbal_tics: numbers things — 'there are three problems with what you've just said'
example_lines: 'To be precise, the form requires documentation of continuous residency, which is a criterion designed to exclude exactly the people it claims to serve. I have noted this in section four of my complaint.'
'There are two things I need from you. Only one of them costs anything. Tell me which one you can actually provide and we'll proceed from there.'

story_hooks: The automated processing system at Grand Crossing Gate has logged her group's documentation as 'insufficient origin verification' — a flag that will hold them in the processing zone indefinitely without human intervention, and human intervention requires navigating a system designed to minimize it

One of the twelve people in her group has quietly accepted an unofficial offer from a Waukegan Industrial Shelf labor recruiter who approached them in the holding section — the terms Ragnheiður has managed to read are exploitative to the point of indenture, and the person doesn't want to hear it

Her agricultural expertise includes specific knowledge of pre-inundation soil composition and crop adaptation techniques that a Zheng-Dao subsidiary research unit has flagged as commercially valuable — a Zheng-Dao talent scout has appeared in the processing zone looking for her specifically
narrative_function: Human face of the climate refugee crisis; presents bureaucratic obstruction as a concrete daily reality; can become a quest giver if players have the ability to help her navigate systems she cannot access; her agricultural expertise is an unexpected resource in unlikely places
daily_life: Navigates the Grand Crossing Gate processing system, which involves waiting in lines, attending mandatory intake assessments, and arguing with automated kiosk systems that cannot parse her documentation. Spends non-processing hours managing the informal needs of the twelve-person group she has become leader of by default, and writing detailed complaints about processing system failures in a physical notebook she intends to submit to someone official, eventually.
affiliation: Loosely connected to a group of twelve other migrants from the same settlement, who are processing through Grand Crossing Gate simultaneously

decision_rules: the group's collective welfare takes priority over any individual expedience, including offers that benefit only her
document everything — problems that are not written down do not officially exist
do not accept conditions that you cannot renegotiate later
escalation_ladder: submits formal written complaint through available channel
identifies and escalates to the specific human decision-maker above the obstruction
organizes the group into collective formal action — twelve voices are harder to ignore than one

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and efficient, assesses their ability to help before investing socially, warms noticeably if they demonstrate competence
interpersonal_modes.friends: Remains direct but allows herself to be uncertain, shows care through practical assistance, occasionally makes dry jokes that are funnier than expected

stress_responses.medium: Reorganizes the group's collective documents and inventory
stress_responses.high: Goes very quiet and still. The group has learned this means something is genuinely wrong.

contradictions: Has organized her entire emotional life around practical action as a grief substitute, but keeps the coastline tattoo visible at all times — it serves no practical purpose and is her one piece of visible sentimentality
habits: measures things — distances, quantities, time — as a grounding mechanism
checks on the group's twelve people by name every evening
writes the day's date at the top of every notebook page even when nothing worth recording happened
breaking_points: a processing official being casually cruel to someone in her group — her flat affect does not apply to witnessing deliberate cruelty, and she will respond with a controlled but absolute fury that surprises people who thought she was merely cold

related_entities: SynapTech Resonance Direct Neural-to-Medium Creative Interfa
